home_title: Which ISP holds up best in a match, near you?
home_lead: The GameRoute barometer compares ISPs on real matches, for every game and every country: how many go without an incident, latency, loss and the peak-hour effect, in an area around you.
filter_zone_note: Areas follow the number of players: about 5 to 10 km in cities, up to 50 to 100 km where players are scarce. They will open with the first data.
filter_games_note: A few examples among the recognised games. The app recognises new ones with every release.
filter_games_none: No game in this list matches.
ranking_sample_help: An ISP is ranked from {players} players and {matches} matches over the period. One person counts as one player, whatever their number of matches.
source_game_help: A value the game measures and reports itself. GameRoute passes it on unchanged.
source_probes_help: Measured by GameRoute probes, one per second, to the server or to the last router that answers.
ranking_empty_title: Collecting data for {game} in this country.
ranking_empty_text: No ISP has {players} players and {matches} matches of {game} over the period yet. The ranking will appear as soon as one ISP reaches that threshold.
ranking_empty_progress: Players measured for this choice: {count} of {required} needed per ISP
ranking_empty_cta: Install GameRoute and turn on anonymous statistics to help complete the ranking.
ranking_legend: Bars on a 0 to 100 % scale, the mark shows the 95 % confidence interval. An ISP is tied with the one above when their intervals overlap. An ISP is ranked from {players} players and {matches} matches in the area.
aside_game_ping: This game reports its own ping. GameRoute shows it labelled “measured by the game”, next to its own network measurements.
aside_no_ping: This game does not report its ping. GameRoute shows the network latency it measures itself, and says how far it goes: to the server, or to the last router that answers when the server ignores probes.
aside_clean_text: The share of matches GameRoute judged good from start to finish: no loss, jitter or latency rise beyond the thresholds, from the player’s home to the furthest point it can measure. It applies to every game.
zones_text: When a match has an incident, GameRoute finds the part of the network where it starts. The share of each part will be published as soon as collection allows.
zones_label: Share of incidents by part of the route, collecting data
zones_note: Share of incidents, not of matches.
how_probe: The GameRoute app measures each match while it is played, one probe per second, and reads the game’s ping when the game provides it.
how_opt_in: Only matches from players who turned on anonymous statistics count. Their location is reduced to an area several kilometres wide on their PC, before anything is sent.
how_bias: These players are not drawn at random: people with problems install a diagnostic tool more often. The barometer compares ISPs with each other, it does not give an absolute truth.
add_text: The app is free and open source, for Windows 10 and 11. During the match it tells you whether a problem comes from your home, your ISP, transit or the server, and produces a report you can send to your ISP.
dl_lead: For Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. Free, no account, no ads.
dl_cta_note: The link opens the latest release on GitHub. Take the file ending in x64-setup.exe.
dl_does_service: It installs the GameRoute capture service, which records the server address when a recognised game connects. Windows asks for administrator permission for this step.
dl_does_nothing_sent: It creates no account and sends nothing. Report sharing and anonymous statistics stay off until you turn them on.
dl_platforms: Linux and macOS are not supported yet.
dl_not_default: Nothing leaves your PC until you share a report or turn on anonymous statistics.
dl_not_location: Neither your IP address nor your postal address in anonymous statistics: your location is reduced to an area several kilometres wide on your PC, before anything is sent.
dl_not_free_text: No free text in a shared report: measurements, operator names and the game name.
dl_smartscreen_text: The installer is not digitally signed yet. Until it is, Windows SmartScreen reports it as coming from an unknown publisher.
dl_smartscreen_meaning: This message does not say the file is dangerous, only that Windows does not know its publisher yet.
dl_smartscreen_notice_body: The message appears when the installer starts. Here is how to continue.
dl_smartscreen_step_check: Check that the file name ends in x64-setup.exe and that the publisher is “Unknown publisher”.
dl_req_rights_value: Administrator, once, to install the capture service
dl_uninstall_how: Open Windows Settings, then Apps, choose GameRoute and click Uninstall. The capture service is removed with the application.
dl_uninstall_data: Your sessions stay on your PC until you uninstall. Report links already shared expire on their own after 90 days.
method_lead: How the barometer is computed, where each figure comes from and what we cannot measure.
method_code_public: The code that applies this method is public.
method_indicators_text: The barometer compares ISPs on matches played by people who installed GameRoute and turned on anonymous statistics. The app measures each match while it is played. The site publishes aggregates per ISP, game, country, area and period, never a single match or player.
method_clean_def: Share of matches judged good from start to finish: no loss, jitter or ping rise beyond the status thresholds, from the player’s home to the server or the last router that answers. Valid for every game.
method_ping_def: Median and 95th percentile of the ping the game measures itself, only for games that provide it. For the others, the column shows “not provided by this game”.
method_ping_source: The game, for example the League of Legends netstats file or the VALORANT client region ping
method_loss_def: What the game says about it, when it does: lost packets for League of Legends, loss episodes per hour of play for VALORANT. These measurements do not compare across games.
method_latency_def: Measured by GameRoute for every game, always naming the point measured: “18 ms to the server”, or “at least 18 ms to the last router that answers” when the game server does not answer probes.
method_jitter_def: Variation in latency from one probe to the next, up to the last router that answers.
method_peak_def: Matches without incident started between 8 and 11 pm, minus those from the rest of the day, in points. Local time of match start.
method_zones_def: Share of incidents by the part of the route where they start: the player’s home, the ISP, transit, server side.
method_never_text: a latency that stops before the server presented as the server ping, a region beacon estimate presented as the game ping, the city of a server when it cannot be established.
method_sources_text: Every value carries its source, in the app and in shared reports. A value never changes label from one screen to another.
method_src_probes_what: One probe per second to each router on the route, during the match. Latency, loss and jitter of each router that answers.
method_src_probes_example: 17 ms to the server, or at least 17 ms to hop 8 (Transit A) when the server does not answer probes
method_src_game_what: The ping the game measures itself, when it provides it: for example the League of Legends netstats file or the VALORANT logs. Many games do not provide it.
method_src_beacon_what: A publisher server that answers pings, in the region the game announces. It gives an order of magnitude, not the ping of your server.
method_src_capture_what: The game server address and port, recorded by the capture service when the game connects.
method_samples_period: The period is the calendar month. The quarter is used for combinations too small over a month.
method_samples_min: An ISP is ranked for a game in an area from {players} players and {matches} matches over the period.
method_samples_below: Below that, the row shows “collecting data” and the number of players already measured, for example “12 of 30 players needed”.
method_samples_person: One person counts as one player, whatever their number of matches.
method_samples_ci: Each share of matches without incident is published with its 95 % confidence interval, computed by grouping matches per player. Two ISPs whose intervals overlap are ranked as tied.
method_reliability_low_def: Beyond ±3 points. The value is published, with this label.
method_zones_text: The barometer works in every country. The ISPs offered depend on the country chosen. Within a country it does not use administrative regions: it divides the territory into areas whose size follows the number of players.
method_zones_size: In cities, areas are about 5 to 10 km wide. Where players are scarce, they grow up to 50 to 100 km, so that each area reaches the minimum number of players.
method_zones_local: A player’s location is worked out on their PC, then reduced to a grid cell before anything is sent. The IP address and postal address are never sent.
method_zones_precision: Precision does not go below about 5 to 10 km, and is often coarser: an IP address sometimes places a subscriber tens of kilometres from home.
method_bias_self: The players measured selected themselves. People with connection problems install a diagnostic tool more often: incident rates are probably higher than across all subscribers.
method_bias_compare: This bias should affect every ISP. The barometer therefore compares ISPs with each other, for the same game and area. Its figures are not an absolute truth about a network.
method_bias_home: Incidents that start at the player’s home (Wi-Fi, router) count in matches with an incident. They weigh on every ISP, and the breakdown by part of the route shows them separately.
method_bias_small: A poorly represented ISP has a wide interval. Check the reliability before drawing conclusions.
method_limits_text: These limits come from the network itself. When a value depends on them, the app and the reports say so.
method_limit_silent: The ping of a server that ignores probes
method_limit_silent_text: The servers of some games, VALORANT and League of Legends for example, answer no probe. The trace stops at the last router that answers, often at a transit provider. We then write the point measured, never a server ping. The real ping comes from the game when it provides it, labelled “measured by the game”.
method_limit_city: The city of a game server
method_limit_city_text: Its address does not say where the machine is, and geolocation databases are often wrong for these networks. Only the region announced by the game is shown.
method_limit_return_text: A probe measures the round trip. The return can go through other operators than the outbound path, and the trace does not see them. A rise attributed to transit can therefore come from the return.
method_limit_cause_text: We see where a slowdown starts, not why. Congestion, maintenance and route changes look alike from outside.
method_limit_home_text: We see loss at the first hop, not its cause. While the router loses packets, the rest of the route cannot be judged.
method_limit_load: The load of the game server
method_limit_load_text: An overloaded server can answer as fast as before. Its internal slowdowns do not show on the network.
method_limit_beacon_text: A region beacon measures another publisher server in the same region. Its value is always labelled “estimate”.
report_text: This link leads to no report. A report link expires after 90 days, and the person who shared it can delete it earlier from GameRoute.
